# T0A-1: A stand-in older MCP server that asks the user two questions

**Status:** In progress · **Progress:** ▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱ 0 of 5 capabilities · **Updated:** 2026-11-20

> A small test server that speaks the older MCP 2025-11-25 protocol and, during one tool call, asks the user two questions in a row. It is the realistic counterpart Tributary must bridge in its first feasibility check.

## Scope

**Roadmap task:** T0A-1 · Finish the legacy 2025-11-25 HTTP test server in `tributary-spike` with a tool that elicits twice

Tributary's hardest promise is carrying a question that an older MCP server asks in the middle of a call across to a client on the new protocol, and the answer back. Before that can be tried, the team needs a dependable older server that actually asks such questions. This task provides it: an order-placing test tool that asks how many items and which shipping option, so the first feasibility check (Gate A) has a real, repeatable counterpart to bridge.

### In scope

- A test server, runnable on its own, that speaks the older MCP 2025-11-25 protocol over HTTP.
- One order-placing tool that asks the user two questions, one after the other, before it answers.
- Clear, distinct outcomes when the user declines or dismisses a question, gives an unusable answer, the client cannot ask questions, an answer comes back as an error, or no answer arrives in time.
- Automated tests that show each of these outcomes against the official MCP Java client.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Non-goals**
>
> - The new-protocol front that Tributary puts in front of this server, and the bridging itself: roadmap tasks T0A-3 and T0A-4.
> - Driving the server through an official new-protocol client and recording the wire trace: roadmap tasks T0A-5, T0A-7 and T0A-10.
> - Choosing or upgrading the MCP Java SDK version: roadmap task T0A-2. This task uses the version already pinned.
> - Anything a Tributary user would run: the server is a test fixture in the feasibility spike and is never published.

## Capabilities

▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱▱ 0 of 5 tasks checked

- [ ] The test server runs on its own and accepts clients of the older MCP 2025-11-25 protocol over HTTP <a id="T0A-1-1"></a>
- [ ] A client sees one order-placing tool, and calling it asks the user two questions in a row before the order is confirmed <a id="T0A-1-2"></a>
- [ ] Declining or dismissing either question ends the call with a clear message naming the question <a id="T0A-1-3"></a>
- [ ] An unusable answer, an error in place of an answer, or no answer in time ends the call with a clear message instead of hanging <a id="T0A-1-4"></a>
- [ ] A client that cannot ask the user questions gets a clear message rather than a hidden failure <a id="T0A-1-5"></a>

## Compatibility

Nothing changes for existing users: there is no released version yet, and the test server lives in the feasibility spike, which is never published.
